telemetry_off_switch.answer: In the app: turning off Settings > General > Automatically check for updates stops the scheduled, counted update checks; a manual Check for Updates still asks the feed. The optional relay is used only after the user pairs a device.

limitations: Privacy policy hang log under2MB differs from pinned README about20MB. Cloud/provider handling is separate.
contradictions: Privacy policy (recovery-privacy) says hang log under2MB; pinned README (readme) describes about20MB across rotated files.

evidence.title: Yardlet privacy policy: online services and their counts (last updated 2026-11-25)
evidence.locator: summary (no analytics; online services keep anonymous counts); update feed section (Cloudflare Worker daily count by version and Mac architecture); download link; feedback; relay
evidence.finding: Yardlet has no analytics and does not send user data to its developer, but its online services keep anonymous counts of the requests they answer. For each update-feed check, a Cloudflare Worker adds one to a daily count for that Yardlet version and Mac architecture. Downloads are counted by link placement and architecture, feedback is sent only when the user chooses, and the optional relay counts connections.

evidence.title: Yardlet update checks and their Settings switch at commit 3db192d
evidence.locator: Sources/NativeHarnessClient/Platform/macOS/YardletSparkle.swift lines 25-35 (Settings switch is Sparkle's automatic-check setting, on by default via SUEnableAutomaticChecks; off schedules no check); Sources/NativeHarnessClient/Domain/YardletSettings.swift line 544 (General: Automatically check for updates); README.md lines 96-103 and 135-137
evidence.finding: Released builds check yardlet.app's appcast automatically, since Sparkle's automatic checks are on by default; the daily check sends Yardlet's and Sparkle's versions in its user agent. Turning off Settings > General > Automatically check for updates schedules no checks until the user picks Check for Updates.
